thread:
mike (oncall): 🚨 Seeing a sudden spike in 5xx from hosted API since the deploy at ~09:12 UTC. Customer tickets piling up. Full dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/alerts/6331

sre-bot: automated alert — 5xx-rate up 18% in last 5m, p95 latency +1.2s, affected route: /v1/generate

alice (sre): on it. Can you paste a couple of sample error IDs / request IDs from logs?

mike (oncall): got a few: req=abc123,cid=us-west-2; req=def456,cid=eu-west-1. Errors are 502/504 gateway timeouts and a handful of 500s with "upstream: read timeout".

jess (support): Customers reporting timeouts + some auth failures (401) when retrying. Escalations: two enterprise customers have active incidents. cc @carmen (sales)

carmen (sales): Thanks @jess — please ping me if any of the enterprise SLAs are at risk. I told them we're triaging.

ben (eng-runtime): suspect this is related to the canary that changed the prefetch/batching selector. Canary name: canary/prefetch-v2-2026-03-18. Rolling back now?

omar (edge): I see a config change pushed to router config that widened scope of "enable-prefetch-v2" from canary-only to global due to a selector typo. That would cause extra load and different cache TTLs.

alice (sre): ok put a hold on further deploys. Ben — can you confirm the exact config key and whether it's binded to the routing matrix?

ben (eng-runtime): config key is feature.prefetch_v2.enabled. In the patch the selector block missed the "namespace: staging" constraint, so the router treated it as global. Patch diff: ```- selector: {namespace: staging}
+ selector: {}
```

mike (oncall): reproducer curl for a failing request (from eu-west): ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -i``` response: 504 after 10s.

jess (support): enterprise customer noticed billing anomalies too — lots of retries and duplicate usage. We should flag billing so they aren't charged for the spike.

carmen (sales): escalate billing credit for impacted customers. I'll collect names.

alice (sre): action list: 1) stop canary rollout; 2) rollback config to previous selector; 3) route traffic off the affected pool; 4) unblock retries and reconcile billing. Who can do the rollback?

ben (eng-runtime): I'm rolling the config back now (started at 09:27 UTC). Rolling change: revert the selector to include namespace. Pushing patch now.

sre-bot: deploy job #4578 started by ben. CI checks passed.

omar (edge): while rollback is applying, I'm going to drain the new runtime pool (pool-id: rp-42) and route traffic to rp-41. Drain in progress — ETA ~45s.

mike (oncall): I've temporarily bumped the shedder threshold for /v1/generate to reduce tail latency for small requests.

alice (sre): please attach sample logs for one 500 with stack trace. We need to confirm if auth tokens were truncated or if the gateway timed out waiting for kernel compilation.

ben (eng-runtime): sample error log (from rp-42): ```2026-03-18T09:20:19Z ERROR handler.go:142 request_id=abc123 upstream_error="upstream: read timeout" kernel_init_time=2.1s kvcache_miss=true auth_ok=true``` Looks like kernel init + kvcache miss pushing request past timeout for some sessions.

mike (oncall): noticed a correlation with long sequences — p99 seq len jumped due to batching change. That fits.

jess (support): sharing repro steps with customers: 1) call /v1/generate with long input 2) set max_tokens high 3) observe timeout >9s. They're asking for mitigation steps until fixed.

alice (sre): mitigation: 1) reduce shedder timeout to 7s for the affected pool 2) enable fallback to smaller model variant for requests with seq>1024 3) advise customers to retry with exponential backoff. We'll coordinate.

ben (eng-runtime): rollback confirmed applied at 09:31 UTC and routers reloaded. RP-42 is draining. Monitoring shows 5xx rate dropping.

sre-bot: deploy job #4578 completed successfully.

omar (edge): rp-42 drained, traffic back to rp-41. p95 latency trending down.

mike (oncall): 5xx rate back to baseline in us-west; eu-west still slowly decreasing.

jess (support): I've messaged the affected customers with a temporary mitigation and that we're issuing credits. They want an ETA — can we provide an incident summary?

carmen (sales): please include root cause: mis-scoped config selector caused global enable of prefetch-v2 which increased kernel init and cache misses, leading to timeouts and retry-related billing spikes.

alice (sre): I'll draft a short incident blurb and a postmortem ticket. Action owners: ben=runtime fix & stricter deploy checks, omar=router guard rails, mike=shedder tuning & SLO notes, jess=billing & customer comms.

ben (eng-runtime): also adding a CI lint that rejects empty selector objects for feature flags — PR incoming.

mike (oncall): thanks everyone. Keep this thread updated with customer reactions and any regression in the next 2 hours. :thumbsup:

jess (support): customers acknowledged. Two have asked to be contacted when credits are applied. I'll follow up once finance confirms.

alice (sre): last check at 09:45 UTC — metrics stable. Opening postmortem ticket: https://pm.internal/redwood/incidents/633123.

mike (oncall): closing the live escalation — will reopen if new spikes. Good triage.
